domain_restrictions: a and b are integers with 0 <= a <= b.
r and j are nonnegative integers.
I is the finite set of integers from a+1 through b.
The index s ranges over I in the product and in the sum over S.
S is any subset of I.
lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I, with repetition allowed through multiplicity.
wt(lambda) is the sum of the multiset elements counted with multiplicity.
The condition wt(lambda) plus the sum over s in S of (r+s) equals j is exact, not approximate.
The product is finite, and if a equals b then it is an empty product.
q is treated as a formal power series variable rather than a numerical parameter.
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every choice of integers a, b, r, j with 0 <= a <= b and r, j nonnegative, if I is the set of integers from a+1 through b and X_j is the set of all pairs (S, lambda) where S is a subset of I and lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I satisfying wt(lambda) plus the sum over s in S of (r+s) equals j, then the coefficient of q^j in the finite product over s in I of (1 - q^(r+s)) divided by (1 - q^s) is equal to the sum over all pairs in X_j of (-1) to the size of S.
quantifier_order: For all integers a, b, r, j satisfying 0 <= a <= b, r >= 0, and j >= 0.
Define I from a and b as the set of integers from a+1 through b.
Define X_j from a, b, r, j as the set of all pairs (S, lambda) with S a subset of I and lambda a finite multiset of elements of I such that wt(lambda) plus the sum over s in S of (r+s) equals j.
Then the coefficient of q^j in the finite product over s in I of (1 - q^(r+s)) divided by (1 - q^s) equals the signed sum over X_j.

variables.domain: the integers from a+1 through b
variables.name: I
variables.role: index set for the product and for the combinatorial objects

variables.name: S
variables.role: subset witness in each admissible pair

variables.domain: finite multisets whose elements lie in I
variables.name: lambda
variables.role: multiset witness in each admissible pair

variables.name: s
variables.role: index variable in the product and in the subset sum

variables.domain: pairs (S, lambda) satisfying the subset and weight condition for the fixed parameters a, b, r, j
variables.name: X_j
variables.role: admissible pairs counted in the signed sum

witness_dependencies: Each admissible witness pair (S, lambda) is constrained by the fixed parameters a, b, r, and j through the set I and the equality wt(lambda) plus sum over s in S of (r+s) equals j.
There is no separate existential witness in the final identity beyond choosing a pair (S, lambda) from X_j.
The sign of each contribution depends only on the size of S, not on lambda.

statement_nl:
Let a, b, r, j be integers with 0 <= a <= b, r >= 0, and j >= 0. Set I := {a+1, a+2, ..., b}. Define X_j to be the set of all pairs (S, lambda) such that S is a subset of I, lambda is a finite multiset of elements of I, and wt(lambda) + sum_{s in S}(r+s) = j, where wt(lambda) denotes the sum of the elements of lambda. Then
[q^j] product_{s=a+1}^b ((1 - q^(r+s)) / (1 - q^s)) = sum_{(S,lambda) in X_j} (-1)^{|S|},
where |S| is the cardinality of S.
